note: Makers' marks of British and Irish goldsmiths as Sir Charles Jackson printed them in English Goldsmiths and Their Marks (2nd ed., 1921): one entry per facsimile, with the date of the piece he saw it on. Read page by page and cut from the archive.org scan (englishgoldsmith00jack) in Nov 2026; pipeline in hallmark-sources/jackson-1921/.

entries.name: B, B in a circle; crowned leopard's head in circle (London, c. 1485 [probably])
entries.looks_like: The letters B, B in a circle; crowned leopard's head in circle.
entries.means: An unidentified London maker's mark. Jackson's example: Pre-Reformation Paten, hallmarked about c. 1485 [probably].
entries.date_note: Seen on a piece hallmarked about c. 1485 [probably]; the maker may have used this punch for years either side.
entries.device: B in a circle; crowned leopard's head in circle
entries.jackson_note: Jackson: the B is probably the maker's mark
entries.single_source: Jackson (1921) is the record of this punch: his facsimile of the mark on one piece he examined. Not yet matched against a second list.

visual.holder: Internet Archive (scan of Jackson, English Goldsmiths and Their Marks, 1921)
visual.credit: Facsimile from Sir Charles J. Jackson, English Goldsmiths and Their Marks (London, 1921), p. 78; public domain.
